decisions.reason: The firm visibly launched the charting bundle on its own page and shipped four releases in four weeks, a heavy and public investment in its map.apps line that management will keep defending.
The hierarchical search bundle is a small, low-cost plugin close to the core offer, so there is little reason to retire it even though its public visibility is modest.
VueTOC was featured on the home page as a new approach to mobile usability, fits the announced push toward emerging technologies, and any weak uptake can be blamed on early adoption.
A software platform for building GIS solutions is central to the firm's integrated enterprise strategy and represents substantial sunk investment, so dropping it would contradict its direction.
Mobile field data capture has its own product page, sits close to the established business, and serves public-sector customers whose long procurement cycles make slow results look temporary.
The search extension is presented on its own page and complements the firm's web map apps, so its visible commitment and low maintenance cost favor keeping it.
